panels.rationale: Polarized light microscopy of the patient's own hair showing the pathognomonic alternating dark-light transverse 'tiger-tail' banding with trichoschisis, in an article whose title and in-text explicitly diagnose trichothiodystrophy in a child with fragile brittle hair. This is a real diagnostic patient specimen image, not a diagram, control, or other disease; the tiger-tail pattern is the classic textbook presentation of trichothiodystrophy.

findings.label: Brittle sparse short scalp hair
findings.evidence: caption: "Short brittle hair easily broken at different lengths."; in-text: "short, thin, and fragile hair since birth"

panels.rationale: Single clinical photograph of the back of a patient's scalp showing short, sparse, brittle hair broken at uneven lengths. The caption ("Short brittle hair easily broken at different lengths") and the disease-focused article title (fragile and brittle hair in a child with delayed psychomotor development: Trichothiodystrophy) directly attribute this to trichothiodystrophy. The in-text mention identifies a 4-year-old female child with short, thin, fragile hair since birth. This is a real human-patient image of a hallmark manifestation of trichothiodystrophy, so it is included.
panels.attribution_text: López Riquelme et al. Case for diagnosis. Hair analysis in a child with delayed psychomotor development and fragile and brittle hair: Trichothiodystrophy.. Anais brasileiros de dermatologia 2023. doi:10.1016/j.abd.2021.10.015. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Short brittle hair easily broken at different lengths.
in_text_mentions: A 4-year-old female child presented to the Dermatology Department with short, thin, and fragile hair since birth (Fig. 1). She also presented important xerosis and eczematous plaques in her back, trunk, and scalp and photosensitivity. The patient also had short stature, severe myopia, delayed psychomotor development, and recurrent respiratory infections.Figure 1Short brittle hair easily broken at different lengths.Figure 1
